title: systems as sci-fi bodysuits
content:
explore my new course, creative systems

in my most recent zine, I wrote that systems are like ships — handmade vessels that carry us from one place to another in the landscape of our creative lives. but, the more I think about it, the more I prefer this metaphor of the system as the sci fi body suit: molded to the shape of an individual creative body, attuned and enhancing its ways of breathing and moving.

you know how, in Dune, the Fremen wear stillsuits that help them retain their body’s moisture — recycling their sweat so as to be as water efficient as possible as they travel through the desert terrain? without a stillsuit, they would die from heat and dehydration.

a system is the same thing. a system’s purpose is to save us from exhaustion and over-exertion. a system is all about forward motion — getting us, in our naked creative bodies, from point A to point B — not necessarily in a linear way, but in the most efficient way. the most efficient way for you is not necessarily the most efficient way for me. this is why it’s a body suit, not a car.



features of a body suit system

a body suit is simulanteously:

  • adaptation/protection — from the outside world, or from unwieldly inner weather

  • filtration — boundaries against information, over-stimulation, and psychic debris

  • intuition/strength enhancement — amplifying natural powers and intuition

  • feedback/insight — providing real time feedback on creative health & energy

  • energy efficiency — recycling and distributing resources in the most efficient way possible

  • regeneration/healing — containing mechanisms for self-repair, rest, and integration

underlying core needs

each body suit is personalized to the wearer, but all humans have basic needs that body suit systems must fulfill —

  • to feel comfort — against perfectionism, pressure, self-doubt, stress

  • to breath — to be in creative respiration and flow within/without

  • to move — through projects, through space, and through time

  • to communicate — signals of when to move vs. rest.

  • to heal — to identify wounds, and tend to them

  • to adapt — to changing inner and outer conditions


perhaps it’s the last one that’s most important — adaptation. the purpose of a system is that it is a skin-tight sheath for your entire creative body, monitoring your vital signs and creative/digestive processes, and sending tiny pulses of electricity to communicate with you — on what to do next. where to go from here. how to transition.

your system body suit is highly intelligent, and evolving — but it does so because you program it to evolve. it is molded to your body — and serves you in more increasingly more sophisticated and evolved ways — but at the same time, it also exists outside of you. you can step away from it, and look at it as a separate entity.

how to begin

before you can create your own body suit, you have to look at your creative body — exactly as it is — naked.

where is your creative body right now? where does it live, in your physical body?

what paradigms or systems is it stuck in — that may or may not be serving it?

I spent years trying to fit my creative body into standardized vehicles (aka, traditional productivity systems) — only to feel tortured, insufficient, and ultimately stranded on the highway, paralyzed and confused about where I’m supposed to go. I talk about this in my podcast episode, transcendence of a productivity addict.

so, the first step is getting out of those vehicles.

then, looking at the creative body — listening to it, sensing into it, asking it what it needs to be comfortable in its own skin.

  • how does it feel, in each moment?

  • where does it desire to go?

  • how does it want to move?

  • how does it wants to be nourished, along the way?

  • how does it want to rest?

all of these are simple questions. but, the ongoing and changing answers to these form the foundations of systems that feel like sci fi body suits — and not self-imposed prisons.

the body wants a system

part of the work is trusting that the creative body wants to make a system body suit. it wants to be more efficient, protected, and supported. it wants a boundary to help it relate to the world.

it definitely won’t be created in a day, or a week. it won’t know the entire journey roadmap, or how it’ll get there — but, at the very least, it’ll give a small, electric signals to tell you yes, keep going and no, stop. it’ll give tiny tugs to pull you in the right next direction.

the body suit as system forms from the boundaries of where the naked skin meets the world. it will start as something very lightweight and small. even this is radical. then, it will evolve from there — into something that can truly feel native to your nature — and magical.
